item.title: Stars’ Miro Heiskanen suffers upper-body injury in win vs. Capitals
item.description: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Stars’ Miro Heiskanen suffers upper-body injury in win vs. Capitals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Stars held on for a wild 6-5 victory over the Washington Capitals at Capital One Arena on Tuesday night, jumping out to a 4-0 lead in the second period and weathering a furious late comeback in the cross-conference tilt. But the victory came with an injury concern involving star defenseman Miro Heiskanen, who left with an upper-body injury after taking just one shift in the second period. He took a hit from Caps forward Justin Sourdif and departed shortly afterward, finishing with 9:41 across eight shifts. The Stars didn’t have a concrete update on the 27-year-old after the triumph, but missing the Finn for any length of time would be a significant blow. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Head coach Glen Gulutzan said Heiskanen would be evaluated Wednesday, per NHL.com. No recovery timeline has been announced. Heiskanen entered Tuesday with three goals and 11 points in 14 games — first among team blueliners — while averaging just under 26 minutes of ice time. He has been anchoring the top pairing alongside countryman Esa Lindell throughout the 2026-27 campaign. He’s one of the most important players on the roster; in 2025-26, he was the only player in the National Hockey League to average more than three minutes per game on both the power play and penalty kill. Following an injury-shortened campaign in 2024-25 in which Heiskanen appeared in just 50 games and underwent knee surgery, he bounced back in a big way last season. The former third overall selection in the 2017 NHL Draft amassed 63 points in 77 games in 2025-26 and added another six points in six Stanley Cup Playoff contests as the Stars were defeated by the Minnesota Wild in Round 1. He finished ninth in the NHL in scoring among defensemen and fourth in average ice time at 25:28. He also helped Finland win bronze at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, recording five points in six games. Overall, Heiskanen has managed 357 career points in 566 regular-season games. He signed an eight-year, $67.6 million contract extension with the Stars in July 2021 that runs through the 2028-29 campaign. Dallas returns to action against the Columbus Blue Jackets at Nationwide Arena on Thursday night, the finale of a brief two-game road trip.

item.title: Chelsea star Cole Palmer escaped straight red card against Tottenham, says KMI panel
item.description: Chelsea forward Cole Palmer ought to have been dismissed ten minutes prior to his eventual sending-off against Tottenham, an independent assessment panel reviewing Premier League refereeing and VAR decisions has concluded. Following an altercation between Palmer and Spurs player Mateus Fernandes during the 70th minute at Stamford Bridge on October 24, the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel determined that the England international deserved a straight red card. By a 3-2 majority, the five-member panel decided that referee Chris Kavanagh's initial call on the pitch was mistaken. Three panellists viewed Palmer's challenge on Fernandes as violent conduct warranting dismissal, noting there was "clear contact to the head" along with behaviour deemed "unnecessary, dangerous and made with excessive force". Nevertheless, all five panellists agreed with VAR John Brooks's choice to refrain from advising an on-field review, backing his decision to stand by the original yellow card awarded by the match official. Palmer was ultimately ordered off ten minutes later in the 80th minute after receiving a second booking following a foul on Conor Gallagher. Palmer clahsed with Fernandes resulting in a yellow card (Getty) In a separate evaluation from the same day, the KMI panel judged that Aston Villa ought to have been awarded a spot-kick during their victory against Manchester City after Elliot Anderson tangled with Johan Manzambi. Three members of the panel argued that Anderson made no effort to play the ball and intentionally widened his posture to block Manzambi's path. Although a 3-2 majority felt the VAR was correct not to intervene with a review recommendation, two panel members contended that a clear and obvious error had occurred. According to Premier League figures, 88 per cent of 162 key incidents evaluated by the panel this season were correctly judged on the pitch, matching performance levels from the same phase last year. That accuracy rate rises to 99 per cent once VAR intervention is taken into account. Examining the fixture between Coventry and Fulham, the panel noted that VAR Jarred Gillett should have prompted referee Adam Herczeg to check a late first-half incident, despite agreeing with the ultimate outcome reached on the pitch and in the video room that no penalty be given to Fulham. It noted an impactful hold by Fulham's Calvin Bassey prior to the corner kick being taken, succeeded by an infringement from Coventry's Bradley Thomas-Asante once the ball entered play. The panel accepted that the VAR had properly spotted both offences. In its findings, the panel explained: "In this situation, as Bassey commits an offence before the ball is in play and the holding action of Thomas-Asante met the threshold for a penalty to be awarded, the VAR should recommend an on-field review to allow the referee to consider both holding actions and reach the correct outcome of retaken corner." item.title: Namibia's road to 2027 Cricket World Cup: Qualification pathway, fixtures, results and standings
item.description: Namibia's road to 2027 Cricket World Cup: Qualification pathway, fixtures, results and standings originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . 2KEY TAKEAWAYS: Namibia co-hosts the 2027 ODI World Cup but has not qualified for it. They finished fifth in CWC League 2 and must now play the Qualifier playoff in Nepal from December 4 to 21. Namibia has appeared at one ODI World Cup, in 2003 (hosted by South Africa , Kenya and Zimbabwe ) where they lost all six matches. Why did co-hosts of Namibia not have automatic qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup? South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia will co-host the 2027 ODI World Cup from October 2 to November 21. However, only two of the three are guaranteed a place in it. The reason simply comes down to their membership status. South Africa and Zimbabwe are ICC Full Members and received automatic qualification as hosts. Namibia is an Associate Member and does not receive an automatic place under the current qualification rules. Namibia must qualify through the same pathway as every other Associate side. Namibia will stage six World Cup matches at the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek, three in the group stage and three in the Super Series, whether their own team is involved. MORE: Has any country hosted a Cricket World Cup without qualifying? CWC Qualifiers play-off format: Why Namibia hasn't qualified for the main qualifier yet The first route to the Qualifier was the 2024-2026 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2. item.title: AS Monaco midfielder Denis Zakaria praises Lamine Yamal as ‘the best player in the world’
item.description: AS Monaco midfielder Denis Zakaria praises Lamine Yamal as ‘the best player in the world’ Spain did not need to wait until Lamine Yamal (19) came along to establish themselves as one of the dominant nations in world football. But they have capitalised on his emergence to cement that status even further. For at just 19 years of age, the FC Barcelona forward is one of those players capable of deciding the outcome of a match at will. And whilst many observers already regard him as the best player in the world, just as many of his peers see him in the same light. Starting with AS Monaco’s Denis Zakaria (29). “Playing against Spain is always a nightmare. They deny you the ball and force you to spend your time running. And when you add stars like Lamine Yamal to that team, it makes things even more difficult. He’s the best player in the world,” said the Swiss player on the programme Zack en Roue Libre , recorded ahead of the Ballon d’Or ceremony. Whilst he also regards Kylian Mbappé (27) as a “star” , an “exceptional” player who is likewise among “the best players in the world” – a very select group – Zakaria does not, however, include him in his list of “players who give you so much pleasure” . “If I had to name two who, when I look at them, make me think, ‘Ah yeah, that’s ridiculous’, it’s Michael Olise and Yamal,” he says. “Ousmane Dembélé is also an exceptional player. His season last year was incredible. He 100 per cent deserves his Ballon d’Or.” GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: Alexander Zverev suffers straight-sets defeat in first match as world No 1
item.description: Alexander Zverev endured a disappointing start to his first week as world No 1 as he slumped to a straight-sets defeat to Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters . The German reached the top of the world rankings when they were updated on Monday but lost 7-6(5) 6-2 to the in-form Italian in his first match with his new title, after receiving a bye to the second round of the Masters 1000 event. 29-year-old Zverev led by 5-2 in the first set tie-break before Musetti won six of the last seven points to seal the set, then surged ahead in the second to break for 2-1 and again for a 5-2 lead before serving out victory. Former world No 5 Musetti has endured a difficult 2026 hampered by injuries, beginning when he led Novak Djokovic by two sets in their Australian Open quarter-final, but has come into a purple patch late in the season, winning his first title in four years in Lyon last month. Musetti said: “It’s pretty shocking the level I was able to play in front of Sascha, who was serving really well, especially in the first set. “It was really close. It could have gone both ways. The key was to stay there at 5-2 [in the tie-break]. I played five great points in a row.” The world No 24 has now won eight of his past nine ATP tour matches and set up a third-round meeting with France’s Luca Van Assche. Musetti, a two-time grand slam semi-finalist, landed 29 winners and eight aces over the course of an hour and 40 minutes at Paris’ La Defense Arena. Defeat for Zverev means the German has gone two seasons without a Masters title, with his last coming in Paris in 2024. Earlier on Wednesday Arthur Fils booked his place at the ATP Finals for the first time, becoming the first Frenchman to compete at the year-end tournament in 10 years - the last being Gael Monfils, who retired in a special ceremony in Paris this week.

item.title: Chicago Bears Pass Protection Analysis on the Sack Allowed vs Seahawks
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts at the line against the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the first two games since Caleb Williams returned, the Chicago Bears’ pass protection allowed 4 sacks to the Atlanta Falcons and then 3 to the New England Patriots. It’s not bad, and in context, I thought the pass protection was solid in each game, but it was still a much higher sack rate than a season ago, when he averaged just 1.4 per game. The Seattle Seahawks defense featured 5 players with multiple sacks through their first seven games, and with the Week 8 matchup in loud Lumen Field in Seattle, I figured their defense would get the best of Chicago’s pass protection scheme a few times. But the Bears only allowed 1 sack to Seattle’s vaunted defense, and I’ll break it down right here. Sack 19: 4th Quarter: 2-10-CHI 23 (14:02) (Shotgun) C.Williams sacked at CHI 13 for -10 yards (M.Morris) After Caleb faked to D’Andre Swift, he looked downfield at Luther Burden III (outside the right hash), but he felt pressure off the left so fast because left tackle Theo Benedet was walked back into the pocket. Caleb drifted right and looked to Swift in the left flat, but didn’t have a clear throwing lane. Benedet did a nice job staying between his guy and his quarterback, but the problem was the depth he gave up, so even though his guy didn’t get the sack, he’s the reason this play was blown up. If Benedet offered up just a bit more resistance, Williams could have hit one of his three checkdowns (probably Colston Loveland over the middle), but there wasn’t time to get through his progressions. It looked like Swift was going to chip if Benedet’s guy took an outside rush. He got a small piece of the defender on the way to the flat, but with the Seattle rush end square to Benedet, there wasn’t enough for Swift to hit Benedet set up inside first, then kicked out for the edge defender. In theory, that inside step would normally entice a defender to go around the edge, exposing his outside shoulder for Swift to target on his chip release and leaving Benedet in a good position as the defender redirected his rush inside. But the Seattle defender had his mind made up to bull rush on the play. Benedet likely didn’t expect it and was driven back. Caleb was forced out of the pocket and ended up even with left guard Joe Thuney, who pulled right to block the edge after a Loveland release. Mike Morris (#94) just reached out and grabbed Williams before delivering the belly-to-back suplex. The Bears did a good job mixing up the tempo and identifying the Seattle defenders all night long, which is hard to do Here’s the individual Sackwatch tally after eight games: Caleb Williams – 4.5 Sacks happen – 3 Garrett Bradbury – 3 Theo Benedet – 2.5 Ozzy Trapilo – 2 Jonah Jackson – 1 Colston Loveland – 1 Tyson Bage

item.title: Decision Day: 5 biggest storylines to know before Audi MLS Cup Playoffs
item.description: Decision Day: 5 biggest storylines to know before Audi MLS Cup Playoffs By Charles Boehm The final test of the MLS regular season is nigh: Decision Day. With eight simultaneous 4 pm ET kickoffs across the eastern half of North America and seven 7 pm kicks in the western half, it’s a jam-packed Saturday smorgasbord of soccer. Six Western Conference teams will vie for the final three slots in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs, while nearly everyone in the Eastern Conference’s postseason field still has something to play for , despite having clinched a spot in the dance. Those of us who try to follow everything as it happens in real time – even with the priceless resource of the MLS 360 live whiparound show – tend to feel like kittens watching a tennis match, eyes bobbing back and forth from one development to the next (and back again). It’s a lot to keep track of! To keep you, dear reader, from getting overwhelmed, here’s a quick rundown of the biggest plotlines and questions still to be answered. 1. Will Nashville claim the regular-season points record? Nashville SC have been far and away the best team in MLS in 2026. The Coyotes won the Supporters’ Shield with weeks to spare last month, and have stacked up the most wins, fewest losses, fewest goals conceded, best goal differential and best home record (an unblemished 15W-0L-2D) in MLS – even as they juggled a springtime run to the Concacaf Champions Cup semifinals, along the way beating LIGA MX giants Club América in their own house to become the first MLS team in history to win at mighty Estadio Azteca. Even with all that, Nashville can claim one more milestone this weekend. Thanks to last Sunday's gripping 3-2 comeback victory over Red Bull New York , which drew them level with 2024 Inter Miami ’s highest-ever regular-season points total of 74, these high-octane Coyotes can set a new points record with a draw or a win vs. FC Cincinnati at TQL Stadium (4 pm ET | Apple TV ). Seventh-place Cincy have plenty to play for, too; they will be keen to avoid the Wild Card round, an extra playoff match for the bottom two qualifiers to deal with. We suspect Nashville head coach B.J. Callaghan and his side will go for it, though, especially since they’ll have a chance to rest during the November FIFA international break, which arrives next week. 2. Who gets the Western Conference Wild Card spots? Now for the real make-or-break matter. The LA Galaxy , Portland Timbers and Colorado Rapids currently possess the West’s last three postseason berths; as the old saying goes, they control their own destiny. item.title: Micah Parsons update: Packers star to practice ahead of Patriots game
item.description: The Green Bay Packers have gone the entire 2026 season without star edge rusher Micah Parsons , who has spent months rehabbing a torn ACL and meniscus in his left knee . The injury, suffered Dec. 14, 2025, against the Denver Broncos, required surgery and kept him on the reserve/PUP list through training camp and every game since. Green Bay has managed without him, riding a strong defensive effort to a 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 8. Head coach Matt LaFleur addressed Parsons’ recovery Monday, and the update marks a real step forward. That air yards don’t always translate into real, edible receiving yards is just part of our frustrating little game. We make small bets here and there and hope things break right from week to week and prove our process correct more often than not. It’s not any more complicated than that, even if we desperately want it to be. item.title: Chelsea stunned by Estonian side in Europe
item.description: [Getty Images] Chelsea have been knocked out of the Uefa Youth League by Estonian side Flora Tallinn. In a major upset at Cobham Training Centre on Wednesday afternoon, the visitors twice came from behind to win 3-2 after drawing the first leg on home soil last week. Chelsea opened the scoring through winger Mathis Eboue, who cut inside and scored just 94 seconds into the match. However, winger Sander Alamaa equalised on the break, having scored both of Flora's goals in the first leg. Forward Ibrahim Rabbaj replaced defender Alfie Osborne at half-time and scored within two minutes, getting on the end of a cross from Eboue to restore Chelsea's lead. Yet midfielder Marten Kukkonen levelled again nine minutes later before Alamaa secured the win from the penalty spot after defender Tayo Subuloye conceded a spot-kick in the 78th minute. It was the second penalty Chelsea had conceded across the two legs, having also gone down to nine men in the Estonian capital last week. Chelsea made their remaining four substitutions and created several chances in an attempt to take the tie to extra time. Instead, the two-time winners of Europe's premier youth club competition suffered a shock exit in front of first-team manager Xabi Alonso, with two of his recent debutants Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli and Reggie Watson having both started.
